title: Base-compatible rational residue field of a localized coordinate prime
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, f in R, and 0 <= r <= n natural numbers. Let T be affine n-space over Spec R_f [def-sbc-affine-space, def-weil-ring-localization-away], let pi:T -> Spec R be its structural projection, and t a point. Under the canonical identification T=Spec C for C=R_f[x_1,...,x_n] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], assume the prime of t equals p C + (x_{r+1},...,x_n), where p is the prime of pi(t). Then there is a field isomorphism kappa_T(t) = Frac(kappa_R(pi(t))[u_1,...,u_r]) [def-weil-residue-field] whose composite with the actual structural residue-field map is the constants embedding. This includes r=0 and r=n. No source chart or quasi-finiteness assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 052E (lemma-local-structure-finite-type), first paragraph of proof, affine scheme translation of Tag 0520 (lemma-refined-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra), including the residue field of its prescribed coordinate prime.

proof.text: Let C=R_f[x_1,...,x_n], let p be the image prime in R and K=kappa_R(p). Since the base point lies in Spec R_f, f is outside p. The residue map R -> K extends to R_f -> K, with kernel p R_f: a fraction vanishes precisely when its numerator is in p.

Evaluate C into L=Frac(K[u_1,...,u_r]) by retaining the first r variables and killing the others. First quotient by the last variables, then reduce coefficients modulo p R_f. The quotient is (R_f/p R_f)[u_1,...,u_r], and its map into K[u_1,...,u_r] and then L is injective. Thus the evaluation kernel is exactly the prescribed sum of ideals.

The evaluation sends every element outside the prime to a nonzero element of L, hence extends to its residue field. The field map is injective. Its image contains R/p and its fractions K and all u_i. As a subfield it therefore contains every polynomial and the inverse of each nonzero polynomial. It is all of L, giving an isomorphism. Agreement on R forces agreement on K by the residue-field universal property.

Transport from Spec C to affine space with AffineSpace.SpecIso, and identify affine scheme residue fields with prime-ideal residue fields. Naturality identifies the structural field map from Spec R with the constants map used in evaluation, so the isomorphism is compatible with that actual map. The same construction for r=0 has no variables and returns the base residue field; for r=n no variables are killed.

proof_origin.place: Explicit coordinate residue-field calculation underlying Tags 0520 and 052E, using the residue-field universal property of Algebra Local rings and Tag 00CP.
